name: Zero-Based Budgeting
title: Zero-Based Budgeting
answer: Zero-based budgeting is a planning method where every expense must be justified for each new period, starting from a zero base rather than the previous budget. In the AI accountant context, this page covers how AI supports building budgets from scratch, linking cost drivers to activities, and comparing proposed spending against strategic goals. It includes forecasting revenue and cost lines without relying on historical inertia. The page addresses practitioners who need to reset baselines and allocate resources based on current needs.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Zero-based budgeting runs on financial planning systems, general ledger extracts, and activity-level cost data. AI-assisted implementations typically sit on cloud data warehouses or planning platforms that can ingest line-item detail, headcount, vendor contracts, and operational metrics. The infrastructure must support versioned budget submissions, workflow approvals, and drill-down from summary budget to individual cost justifications.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Practitioners define decision packages for each activity or cost center, rank them by value, and fund from zero upward. AI can help by clustering historical transactions into decision packages, suggesting cost drivers, and flagging unjustified recurring expenses. The work involves iterative reviews where managers defend each package, and algorithms may score packages against strategic priorities or peer benchmarks. The output is a budget built from approved packages rather than prior-year adjustments.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Zero-based budgeting raises questions about who can see and challenge cost justifications, and how AI-generated rankings are audited. Risks include over-reliance on opaque scoring, bias in package ranking, and loss of context for long-cycle investments. Provenance requires clear records of which data and model versions produced each suggested cut or reallocation. Budget owners should retain authority to override automated recommendations, with an audit trail for every change.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Zero-based budgeting is moving from annual exercises to rolling, driver-based reviews where AI continuously re-evaluates cost packages against real-time activity data. Future systems may link zero-based budgets to operational forecasts and automatically propose reallocations when volumes or strategic priorities shift. The practice is likely to become more granular and frequent, with less reliance on fixed annual cycles and more on continuous justification of spend.
